# CIRCT RTL-generation artifacts

What `microarch.py` produces on the **CIRCT** path, as distinct from the Vitis
HLS path (`main`, `examples/accelerator/tinytpu_vitis`) and the Catapult
SystemC path. Kept because the generator is not runnable from a clean checkout:
it needs a CIRCT build, and `tinytpu_*_prj/` is gitignored on this branch as
regenerable output. These files are the part that is not.

## The pin

    // Generated by CIRCT af5369d
    module tinytpu(  // examples/accelerator/tinytpu/microarch.py:149

`af5369d` is the only record of which CIRCT produced this. The clone that built
it (`externals/circt`, 2.3 GB including its build tree) was deleted on
2026-09-18 during the pre-migration cleanup; re-clone at this commit to
reproduce. The flattened top, `tinytpu.sv`, was 14 MB and is **not** kept --
it is regenerable and too large to be useful in git. The per-unit modules are
kept because they are small and they document the interface.

## `manifest.json` is a scheduling model

The part worth keeping. Per module it records a determinacy class, a latency,
and per-port `{bank, factor, latency, width}` descriptors:

| module | determinacy | latency | reads | writes | ops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tinytpu_mxu` | counted_static | 41 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| `tinytpu_vpu` | counted_static | 12 | 3 | 1 | 5 |
| `tinytpu_vload` | counted_static | 9 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tinytpu_vstore` | counted_static | 9 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tinytpu` (top) | **indeterminate** | **none** | 5 | 1 | 0 |
| `tinytpu_dma_load` | **indeterminate** | **none** | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tinytpu_dma_store` | **indeterminate** | **none** | 1 | 1 | 0 |

This bears on `main`'s audit item 22, which found that the Catapult SystemC
fork's `Wire` is wrong in RTL because nothing couples a producer's and a
consumer's counters -- a missing scheduling model. This path has one, and it is
a real answer for the four `counted_static` units.

**It is only a partial answer, and the split is the point.** The top and both
DMA units are `indeterminate` with no latency, which is exactly the
data-dependent case: a VLIW delay line has to schedule against units whose
latency is not known at compile time, and those are the three this model
declines to describe. So the model covers the units that need it least.

`gen_ip.tcl` also pins this path to **fp32** -- it instantiates Xilinx
`add_f32_f32_f32_l2` / `mul_f32_f32_f32_l2` / `cmp_f32_f32_u1_l1` cores for
`xcu55c` -- so it is not matched to the int8 Gemmini comparison on `main`
either.
